candidates.statement: Subpart B—Electronic Records § 11.10 Controls for closed systems. Persons who use closed systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ proce- dures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, when appropriate, the confidentiality of elec- tronic records, and to ensure that the signer cannot readily repudiate the signed record as not genuine. Such pro- cedures and controls shall include the following:
candidates.context: (9) Open system means an environ- ment in which system access is not controlled by persons who are respon- sible for the content of electronic records that are on the system. (a) Validation of systems to ensure accuracy, reliability, consistent in- tended performance, and the ability to discern invalid or altered records.

candidates.statement: (d) Limiting system access to author- ized individuals. (e) Use of secure, computer-gen- erated, time-stamped audit trails to independently record the date and time of operator entries and actions that create, modify, or delete electronic records. Record changes shall not ob- scure previously recorded information.
candidates.context: (c) Protection of records to enable their accurate and ready retrieval throughout the records retention pe- riod. Such audit trail documentation shall be retained for a period at least as long as that required for the subject elec- tronic records and shall be available for agency review and copying.

candidates.statement: § 11.30 Controls for open systems. Persons who use open systems to cre- ate, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ proce- dures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, as ap- propriate, the confidentiality of elec- tronic records from the point of their creation to the point of their receipt.
candidates.context: (2) Revision and change control pro- cedures to maintain an audit trail that documents time-sequenced develop- ment and modification of systems doc- umentation. Such procedures and controls shall in- clude those identified in § 11.10, as ap- propriate, and additional measures such as document encryption and use of appropriate digital signature stand- ards to ensure, as necessary under the circumstances, record authenticity, in- tegrity, and confidentiality.

Subpart C—Electronic Signatures § 11.100 General requirements. (a) Each electronic signature shall be unique to one individual and shall not be reused by, or reassigned to, anyone else.
